title: The reshimu and the Kav: one power to unite and to measure, from the Essence itself
overview:
Chapter 15 gives the *nimshal* of the teacher of chapter 14. The *reshimu* left in the empty place is, for the Kabbalists, the *yud* of *SaG*, *Malchus* of *tevuna*; in plain terms it is the teacher's point, a *hiyuli* that holds everything. The *Kav* drawn from it is *mamash* the infinite light, narrowed only for the receivers. The lower it goes, the more it shows the whole power, and the aim is that the student become a Rebbe himself.

The *Kav* has two opposite powers: it unites everything, and as the *kav hamida* it measures everything apart. Both are true and each depends on the other, like the king who can jail you and pardon you. Really these are not things: it is the *Aibershter*, who can be infinite, zero, or anything between. So He can also break His own plan, with more light (the class trip to NASA, the fireworks at Sinai) or less (the class that sits and does nothing, exile), and we can ask Him to change the will itself. The two powers weigh the same, and even in a kindergarten you get the whole power of the teacher.

sections.title: The reshimu: the yud of SaG, a hiyuli that holds everything
sections.summary: The *nimshal* of the teacher's point is the *reshimu* left in the empty place. In Kabbalistic terms it is the *yud* of *SaG*, *Malchus* of *tevuna*; in plain terms it is a *hiyuli* that holds everything, and it limits the light to a line only for the sake of the receivers.

phrases.he: (טו) והנמשל מכל הנזכר לעיל יובן
בבחינת רושם שנשאר בחלל ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
(שהוא יו"ד דס"ג שבטהירו עילאה
phrases.en: which is the *yud* of the *SaG*; this *reshimu* is the *yud* of the *SaG* into *tehiru ila'a*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בספר עמק המלך)
phrases.en: as it explains in *Emek HaMelech*

blocks.text: Chapter 14 gave the analogy; here is the *nimshal*: the *roshem* left in the *chalal*, the empty place. The parentheses add that this *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*) is **the *yud* of the *SaG* into *tehiru ila'a***, as *Emek HaMelech* explains. What does that mean exactly?

These parentheses are really footnotes, the kind a book today puts at the bottom of the page. And they are like the footnotes in the *Rambam*, not like a *Rashi*: *Rashi* explains what it says, while a footnote in the *Rambam* brings in a whole bunch of extra things and makes it totally more difficult. These are footnotes for the Kabbalists, the very advanced; to understand the book you can skip them entirely. (The student protests that he has explained it anyway, so he explains.)

The basic thing: it is the *daled rabsi*, the big *daled*, *Malchus* of *tevuna* (understanding, as it draws an idea out): the last *yud* of the *SaG*. *SaG* is spelled with *yuds* and an *alef*, ten letters; the four-letter Names, the four levels *ABYA* (*Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*), have ten when expanded.

*BaN* has only nine letters; all the others have ten. The *reshimu* is *Malchus* of *tevuna*, which is exactly what was said of the teacher: when he thinks of what he is going to teach, he has it all down to a point, and from this point come all the explanations. This is also the source of... *AB*, *SaG*, the source of the *shevira* (the breaking) and of the repair.

Spelled out, the Name *Havaya* is made of four Names: *AB*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*. They fold over, it says: *MaH* goes into *AB* and *BaN* into *SaG*. But *BaN* has only nine letters, so the *yud* of the *SaG* is left over.

Why does *BaN* have only nine? Before the *nesira* (the sawing apart), as you learn later, *Malchus* has only nine *sefiros*. *Malchus* of *Malchus* receives from all the other *Malchuyos*, but mainly from the *yud* of *SaG*, *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

So the letters of *dibur* (speech) receive from the letters of *machshava* (thought): "The mother lends the clothes to the daughter." The desire to speak already has all the *middos* (attributes), only not the letters, the five *gevuros*, which come from thought; and thought's letters come from the *yud* of the *SaG*.

The *yud* of the *SaG* as it is to itself, its inner side, is *Malchus* of *bina*; as it goes down, *Malchus* of *tevuna*. It is like the *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a* (the higher and the lower unity), "*Havaya* is one" and "Blessed be the Name", *Atzilus* and *Beriya*; but higher: the *Atzilus* of the whole, where *Adam Kadmon* is the *Beriya* of the whole. From here the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* receives.

The letters of the *reshimu*, which go over from before to after and are *boke'a* (break through) into the *Kav*, have to come from *tevuna*. The *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* breaks through the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu*, and its letters are the letters of speech or of writing: it says the letters on the Tablets are the actual letters of the *reshimu*. But they came from *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and so did the building of *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

But it really does not matter; that is the Kabbalistic manner. The basic thing is "the *nimshal* of all the above": he already explained it to us better than this, the *roshem* that remained in the empty place.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת היולי
phrases.en: That the *reshimu* is a *hiyuli*

phrases.he: כולל כל מה שיסתעף ממנו על ידי הקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: which includes anything which will branch out of it through the *Kav v'chut*

phrases.he: וגם שנתעלם כללות האור העצמות
עד שלא נשאר רק בחינת רשימו,
phrases.en: still there's nothing but *reshimu* left

phrases.he: עם כל זה ודאי הכל נכלל בו בקיצור
על ידי זה הצמצום דווקא
כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like was explained before

blocks.text: The *reshimu* is a *hiyuli* **which includes anything which will branch out of it through the *Kav v'chut***. Even though nothing is left but a *reshimu*, everything is certainly included in it in short. He is recapping here all the way back to chapter 12.

phrases.he: וגם מה שהוא מורה העדר ההתפשטות למטה,
אינו בחינת צמצום גמור
רק מצד שהוא בחינת כח ההיולי כו' כנזכר לעיל
רק להיותו כח מגביל לכללות האור הראשון, על כן בלתי מתפשט רק דרך קו,
phrases.en: Since it's the *koach hamagbil*, that's why the light in it, even when it is *misposhet*, is not *misposhet* in an infinite way like it was before, but only in a *metzumtzam* way, *derech Kav*

phrases.he: לפי אופן ההשפעה כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: according to the *hashpa'a*, which goes according to the *mekabel*

blocks.text: The *reshimu*'s absence of spreading below is not a complete *tzimtzum*. **Since it's the *koach hamagbil*, that's why the light in it, even when it is *misposhet*, is not *misposhet* in an infinite way like it was before, but only in a *metzumtzam* way, *derech Kav***, according to the giving, which follows the *mekabel* (the receiver).

sections.title: The Kav is the infinite light itself, narrowed only for the receivers
sections.summary: The *Kav* has in it the power of the first light, *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*; it comes as a line only because of the receivers. Like the *ish tevuna* who brings it down to the sheep, the lower it goes, the more it shows the whole power, and the aim is that the student become a Rebbe himself.

phrases.he: אמנם יובן מהנזכר לעיל
דקו זה יש בו מכח האור הראשון שלפני הצמצום
בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
רק שבא דרך קו, לפי אופן המקבלים כו'
phrases.en: the only reason it comes because of *Kav* is because of the *mekablim davka*, not because of the *mashpia*

blocks.text: This *Kav* has in it the power of the first light before the *tzimtzum*, *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*. Not only does the *reshimu* itself hold the entire *Ein Sof*: the *Kav* too, as it expands, can be expanded all the way back to the original light.

blocks.title: The Rogatchover talking to his equal
blocks.text: Talking to somebody *mamash* on his own level, like the Rogatchover to another guy like that, not to little students, even the *Kav* is *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*, with the whole *Or Ein Sof* in it. It depends who the *mekabel* is: **the only reason it comes because of *Kav* is because of the *mekablim davka*, not because of the *mashpia*** (the giver).

phrases.he: ובזה יובן מה שכתוב באורך נראה אור
בחינת הארה דהארה הנקרא אור של תולדה
phrases.en: a secondary light, which is called *haara d'haara*, *or shel tolda*

phrases.he: שאחר הצמצום בוקע האור דרך קו בעלמא כו',
phrases.en: it only breaks through in a very *metzumtzam* way, just like a little line of light

phrases.he: אבל הוא בא מאורך העצמי
להיות שברשימו הרי נכלל הכל וממנו נמשך הקו
phrases.en: it's the whole thing of the *reshimu* that goes into the *Kav*, and the *reshimu* has the whole thing of the whole *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: בבחינת היולי לכללות השפע
להיות בבחינת מעלה ומטה על כל פנים,
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים

blocks.text: "In Your light we see light": the explanation for the *mekabel* comes from the actual light of the *mashpia*. Even though it is **a secondary light, which is called *haara d'haara*, *or shel tolda***, a glow of a glow, a light of offspring, it really comes from the original light.

After the *tzimtzum* the light breaks through by way of a mere line: **it only breaks through in a very *metzumtzam* way, just like a little line of light**. But it comes from Your essential light: **it's the whole thing of the *reshimu* that goes into the *Kav*, and the *reshimu* has the whole thing of the whole *Ein Sof***.

blocks.question: The *tevuna* goes according to the receiver; is the light of the *Kav* not according to the receiver?
blocks.text:
He ties "Your essential light" to the *tevuna*. The student reads *me'erech*; the word is not *erech* but "Your light", as in "In Your light we see light". Then the question: the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter* (the One Above) is according to the *mekabel*.

The *tevuna* itself is not: it is the *Aibershter*'s, and everything is in there, though He now puts it into an explanation for the *mekabel*. And even that explanation, made to the *mekabel*'s measure, comes *mamash* from the actual knowledge of the *mashpia*.

Not only that. As was said of Shlomo's three thousand analogies, "the lower down it goes, the higher up it shows": that he can bring it lower, especially in the *tevuna*, shows that there is more of the *etzem* (the essence) there.

blocks.title: The long nun in the Hebrew notebook
blocks.text: That is why the *tevuna* is a long *nun*. Did you ever see the Hebrew notebooks they teach little kids to write in? Not like the English ones, just a bunch of lines: each line has a space on top and on the bottom, and the *lamed* goes up past the line, the *nun* down past it. It goes past its own place into the next level.

That is *tevuna*: the *ish tevuna* (the man of *tevuna*) can *davka* bring it down to the sheep, below his own level, and that shows even more than the *bina* itself what a great *ish tevuna* he is. The lower down it goes, the higher up he is.

So the *Kav*'s going down shows it is the whole *koach* (power) of the *Or Ein Sof*. An explanation is less than how the teacher understands it himself, yet it is an actual light from his own inner light. So the *Kav* is *mamash* the power of the original light, and it can stop being contracted and become the whole of it.

blocks.title: The student will be a Rebbe himself
blocks.text: Not only that: it is not really a *tzimtzum*. The *kavana* (intention) of the *Kav* is not a contracted light, just as the Rebbe does not mean to give the student a little tiny explanation. By the end of the explanations he gets the whole thing, and not only understands like the Rebbe: "he will be a Rebbe himself." So the whole *Atzmus* (the Essence) passes over; the whole *etzem* is in there.

sections.title: Two opposites in the Kav: it unites everything, and it measures everything
sections.summary: The *Kav* includes the left in the right and makes all the unifications, down to a light in a vessel not its own; and it is the *kav hamida*, which measures every light and vessel apart. The power to divide is the same power as the power to connect.

phrases.he: ומזה הטעם יובן תירוץ על
ב' ענינים הפכים שנמצא בקו זה
phrases.en: the two opposites which is in the *Kav*

phrases.he: הא' אשר בכחו דוקא לאכללא שמאלא בימינא כו'
שהוא בחינת ההתכללות והיחודים
של כל האורות המסתעפים מכתר דאדם קדמון עד מלכות דאצילות
עד שעל ידו דוקא יוחלף האור בכלי שאינו שלו,
כמו אור החסד בכלי הגבורה כו'
כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות
phrases.en: This will be explained later, I think it's chapter 21 or 22 or something like that

phrases.he: בענין וא''ו דוהנורא כו'

blocks.text: Two opposites are in this *Kav*. The first: *davka* it has the power "to include the left in the right", all the *hiskalelus* and *yichudim* from *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon* to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, until a light goes into a vessel not its own. **This will be explained later, I think it's chapter 21 or 22 or something like that.**

It is from the *Atzmus*, where it is all one; that is why the *Kav* can include everything together. It has the power of the essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, where these things are totally non-differentiated.

As explained elsewhere on the *vav* of "and the awesome": of "the great, the mighty and the awesome" that we say of the *Aibershter*, "the great", *chesed*, is the *Or Ein Sof*; "the mighty" is the *tzimtzum*; and "and the awesome" is the *Kav*.

phrases.he: והב' מה שנקרא בשם קו המדה דוקא,
למדוד כל אורות וכלים כו'
וכנזכר לעיל בענין הקו שנקרא אמת הבנין כו'
שזהו היפוך ההתכללות לכאורה.
phrases.en: that's the opposite

blocks.text: The second: it is the *kav hamida*, which measures, and measuring means each one is different: by its measurement this one is *chachma* and that one *bina*. And it is *haynu hach*, one and the same: the power to divide is *mamash* the power to connect.
And measuring, **that's the opposite** of the *hiskalelus*: this one is this and that one is that, the right, the left and the middle, "one long, one short and one in between".

sections.title: Both are true, and each depends on the other: the power of the Essence and the power of the reshimu
sections.summary: The one who can keep you out is the one who can let you in. From the Essence in the *Kav* comes the power to unite; from the *reshimu* in it comes the power to measure, and the inner *MaH*, the *kav hamida*, already holds every *midda* the teacher will ever show. But really these are not things: it is the *Aibershter* Himself, who can be in infinite mode, in zero mode, or anywhere in between.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא דשניהם אמת
phrases.en: Really, they're both true. It has both powers.

phrases.he: ואדרבה הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: not only that, just the opposite: the one is connected to the other

blocks.text: **Really, they're both true. It has both powers.** And **not only that, just the opposite: the one is connected to the other**. Because he has the power to separate, he has the power to connect, and because he can connect, he can separate.

blocks.title: The guard at the border and in the prison
blocks.text: At the border, the guy who has the power to keep you out is the same guy who can let you through: it is really the power of the king. The same in a prison. Ask the guard to let you out, and he tells you he doesn't have the power: you have to go back to whoever put you in here, the judge.

blocks.title: The judge only follows the law
blocks.text: Even the judge does not have the power; he only goes by the law. Tell him he put you in here, and he says he didn't: he just does his job, the same as the guard. You broke the law, the law says you go in for a certain amount of time, and "I just followed the law."

blocks.title: Only the king can pardon
blocks.text: So you have to go to the king. He made the law, so he can pardon you even against the law: that is what a pardon means. The judge cannot pardon you; the law put you in, and he only decides according to the law. The originator of the law, who put you in, is the one who can take you out. It is *mamash* the same power: the one who can divide is the one who can connect. The one depends on the other.

phrases.he: משום דשרש זה הקו
מכח הראשון דעצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הוא בא
כנזכר לעיל בענין באורך דוקא נראה אור דקו זה
ובכח האור העצמות דאין סוף
phrases.en: In the power of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: ודאי יש לעשות בחינת התכללות ויחודים של כל ההפכים בכל ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: there's certainly a power to make all the *yichudim* in all the *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: מראש דאדם קדמון כו' עד מלכות דאצילות
וכמאמר אנת הוא דמייחד לון ומקשר לון כו',
phrases.en: you're the one that unifies and ties them together

phrases.he: אנת הוא מלגאו ומלבר כו'
phrases.en: you're from the inside and you're from the outside

blocks.text: The root of the *Kav* is the first power, the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*. **In the power of the *Ein Sof* … there's certainly a power to make all the *yichudim* in all the *hishtalshelus***, because in the *Or Ein Sof* they are all one. As it says, "**you're the one that unifies and ties them together**", "**you're from the inside and you're from the outside**".

phrases.he: וכן ענין שם מ''ה מלגאו
phrases.en: the thing of the *Shem MaH* on the inside

phrases.he: דאיהו אורח כל האצילות כו'
phrases.en: which is the way of the whole *Atzilus*

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: Next, **the thing of the *Shem MaH* on the inside**, **which is the way of the whole *Atzilus***. The Name *MaH* is the line. Of *AB*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, *MaH* is the *vav*: *Zeir Anpin* and the *middos* coming down. And *middos* means the *kav hamida*, which measures.

It comes from the *reshimu*, the *SaG*, and then the line comes down, the Name *MaH*, the path of all of *Atzilus*: not a length, *orach* is a pathway. The light of the line comes down to the end of *Atzilus*. That is the inner *MaH*; the outer *MaH* is another, lower one.

He is not exactly sure how it works, but the *yud* at the head of the *vav* is not the upper one; it is the *yud* at the end of the *SaG*. The *middos* come from *Malchus* of *tevuna*. As you will learn, though they come from *daas*, *chachma* and *bina* are the upper *Abba* and *Ima* and *tevuna* is *Ima tata'a* (the lower mother), because the *middos* come out *davka* from *tevuna*.

So the *kav hamida*: *middos* do not actually mean emotions. They mean measurements, the long, the short and the medium, and so there are really three *middos*, not seven. Seven is the three, then their three reactions, then *Malchus*, the extension of the *middos* to the outside: *Chagas*, then *Nehi*, and the essence of the *middos* is *Chagas*. That is why you learn later of the big *vav* and the little *vav*.

There *Zeir Anpin* is called sometimes Yaakov (and Yisroel) and sometimes Yosef: as *Chagas* it is Yaakov, the attribute of truth, *tiferes*; as *Nehi* it is Yosef, "the righteous one, the foundation of the world". And the outside of *Nehi* is sometimes called Noach.

But the basic thing is the *midda*: a measurement, and that is what a characteristic means. They are called emotions, but they should all be called characteristics: the emotion comes out of the characteristic. A *kaasan* (an angry man), of the *midda* of *gevura*, is not angry right now; he tends to get angry. A *chasdan* is not doing a kindness right now; he has a characteristic of being a kind guy.

The next side opens mid-point. The *Kav* is the inner *MaH*, the *kav hamida*, the line that measures; the outer *MaH* is the *middos* of *Atzilus*. "The path of all of *Atzilus*" means that the whole measurement later in *Atzilus*, in the outer *MaH*, is already included in the inner *MaH* of the *Kav*.

blocks.title: Every midda the teacher will show is already there
blocks.text: In the analogy of the teacher's *hiyuli* for measurement: every characteristic he will show in the day-to-day teaching, the seven days of the week, the "days of the world", is already included in this *kav hamida*. The whole way he is going to act is already there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: A boys' class and a girls' class
blocks.text: It is all there, and he will act differently for different classes, speaking to each in the way that class needs. Give him a boys' class or a girls' class: in a boys' class you need a little more discipline. As the *Aibershter* told Moshe, "speak to the children of Israel" and "say": to the men you have to talk tough, and to the ladies in a nice way.

blocks.title: The geniuses and the ghetto school
blocks.text: Or tell him he is going into a class with the top students in the country, special geniuses, totally motivated; or else into the worst ghetto school there is, where they come with guns and even the five-year-olds carry them. Obviously he will show different *middos*. But it is all already in the inner *MaH*, in the *kav hamida*, and that is what measures, for the different *mekablim*, what kind of a character he will put forth.

blocks.text: It can relate to each *mekabel* from two things: the power of the *Atzmus*, and the *midda*, *davka* from the power of the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* to separate out different things for different people, the opposite of including everything. The Name *MaH* includes both: it is *Zeir Anpin*, *tiferes*, which includes the two sides.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: Up there too, "and the awesome" means the *Kav* is an equal force. It seems otherwise: first the *Or Ein Sof*, the real big force; after the *tzimtzum* only a *reshimu*, somehow lesser; and the *Kav* only what comes out of it, limited, *mamash* a nothing next to the original infinite light. It is not like that.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: "The great, the mighty and the awesome" are right, left and middle, three of the same level. And Yaakov is the choicest of the Avos *davka* because he includes both of them: the *Kav* has both powers in it. It is the middle bar.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: Writing lines, or teaching him everything
blocks.text: The *Kav* can contract all the way down to the *reshimu*: the teacher teaches nothing, makes them all write lines or sit in the corner, even puts a kid outside the class. A total *tzimtzum*. And to an equal he can teach the whole entire thing: the *Kav* can be the whole infinite light. That is "and the awesome", the *tiferes* of the *Or Ein Sof*, which balances the other two.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: And not just the *tiferes* of the *Or Ein Sof*: of the *Maor* (the source of the light). The *Or Ein Sof* is the *chesed* of a higher thing. In this system the *Or Ein Sof* is "the great", the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* "the mighty", the *Kav* "and the awesome". And who is this? "The G-d": the *Aibershter* Himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: "The great, the mighty and the awesome" means the line is not really the line, not the *kav hamida*: "it's the teacher himself." The original thing is the teacher who knows it and contracts the whole thing. "The *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*" just means a power, a description of something the teacher himself did.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.title: The cat's power of movement
blocks.text: There is no such thing as a power of movement. A cat can run because he has the body of a cat; destroy the body and he can't run. You cannot kill the cat and keep his power of movement: "There ain't no power of movement." It just means that he can move.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: It is a very big mistake people make, separating these things into things: the *reshimu* is a thing, the *Kav* is a thing. That is not what it means. It is what chapter 4 said: learned properly, the particulars do not take away from the whole. We are not talking about the *Kav* here at all, or *Atzilus*, or the *Or Ein Sof*, or the *yud* of *SaG*. "We're talking about the *Aibershter*."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

blocks.text: The *Kav* means that the *Aibershter* can measure the *mekabel*. The *Or Ein Sof* means He can be in infinite mode; the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*, that He can be in zero mode; and the *Kav*, that He can be in any mode He wants in between. He can do anything He wants.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 013 opens in the middle of class 012's explanation of line 28 and stays with it until it finishes reading the line at w1519.

phrases.he: הכל הוא מצד הארת אור העצמות דאין סוף שבקו זה,
שהולך ונמשך עד למטה במלכות,
סוף כל דרגין
phrases.en: this thing, that he can spread downwards all the way to *sof kol dargin*

phrases.he: והיא הנותנת
phrases.en: this is the same thing that gives it

phrases.he: דוקא שיש בכחו למדוד מדה וגבול לכל אורות וכלים
ולכל יחוד משפיע ומקבל,
כמה יהיה מ''ד ומ''ן כו'
phrases.en: in terms of different classes, the influence from above and the influence from below: he measures it all

phrases.he: מצד בחינת הרשימו המגביל לכל אור העצמות באופנים שונים
phrases.en: that's the power of the *hagbala*

phrases.he: כמו ששיער בעצמות אור אין סוף לפני הצמצום כו'
phrases.en: these *ofanim meshunim* of the *tzimtzumim*, already *meshuar* before the actual *tzimtzum*

blocks.text: It is all from the light of the Essence of the *Ein Sof* in this *Kav*, drawn down into *Malchus*, the end of all levels: *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, or it could be of *Asiya*.

And **this thing, that he can spread downwards all the way to *sof kol dargin***, is what gives it the power to measure every light, vessel and union of *mashpia* and *mekabel*, how much *mayin duchrin* and *mayin nukvin*: **in terms of different classes, the influence from above and the influence from below: he measures it all**.

From the *reshimu*, which limits: **that's the power of the *hagbala***. Both powers are in the *Kav* as in the Essence before the *tzimtzum*: **these *ofanim meshunim* of the *tzimtzumim*, already *meshuar* before the actual *tzimtzum***. As was said of reaching for the vodka bottle, or of the cat jumping.

phrases.he: ונמצא מצד עצמות האור שבקו
נקרא בחינת היולי ליכלל ולחבר את הכל כו',
phrases.en: it's the *hiyuli* for all the unifications

phrases.he: ומצד כח הרשימו המגביל שבו מגביל שיעור ומדה לכל,
phrases.en: it can make all the *hagbalos* and give a *shiur u'midda* to everything

phrases.he: על דרך אותו בחינת השיעור הראשון שנכלל ברשימו זו
phrases.en: and it can make the *hagbalos* according to the original *shiur* in the *glif glifu*, which was included in the *reshimu*

phrases.he: על דרך משל אומן העושה רושם,
phrases.en: he makes a blueprint

phrases.he: שמגביל האופן של המעשה,
שיהיה הכל מדוקדק כמו שהוחלט השיעור בעצמו
שלא ינטה ימין ושמאל כו'
phrases.en: that he'll not go right or left from the original plan

blocks.text: From the Essence of the light in the *Kav*, **it's the *hiyuli* for all the unifications**; from the limiting power of the *reshimu* in it, **it can make all the *hagbalos* and give a *shiur u'midda* to everything**, by the original *shiur* in the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving), which was included in the *reshimu*.

As a craftsman who makes an outline: **he makes a blueprint**, so that everything comes out exact, **that he'll not go right or left from the original plan**. And he does not have to rethink the whole plan anymore; it is all written down.

sections.title: More than the measure, or less: changes come from the Essence itself
sections.summary: When a light comes that is beyond the *kav hamida*, or when the light is held back, the plan is broken, and only the teacher who made the plan can break it: the trip to NASA, the class that sits and does nothing, the giving of the Torah with all the fireworks, exile. That is why we can ask "from before You" to change the will that made the plan itself.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שאם לפעמים יהיה תוספת אור בנאצלים,
יתר מכפי מאמר קו המדה כו',
phrases.en: different from the *kav hamida*

phrases.he: היינו מכח האור העצמות דוקא
שלפעמים יאיר כך ולפעמים יאיר כך

blocks.text: At times an addition of light comes beyond the word of the *kav hamida*, **different from the *kav hamida***, *davka* from the light of the Essence, which shines sometimes this way and sometimes that. So what is the *kav hamida*?

blocks.title: The class trip to NASA
blocks.text: By the *kav hamida*, the teacher made a class plan: Monday chapter 1, Tuesday chapter 2, Wednesday chapter 3. Say it is a science class, and on Tuesday, instead of chapter 3, he takes them to NASA, or to the museum of science. There they see something way beyond the plan, with no relation to their level; they don't understand what is going on. So what happened to the *kav hamida*? The teacher can do anything he wants.

blocks.title: Then why break the plan?
blocks.text: But there was a plan, so why did he break the *kav hamida*? Because seeing something way beyond their capacity will give the kids a taste for it, so they will want to become scientists. Then it is part of the plan, and of the *kav hamida*? No. The *kav hamida* is according to their measure, and this is not according to their measure at all.

What the student just said is something like a miracle, like the splitting of the Sea: it does not go according to the place and its measure, or the plan of creation. It goes outside of nature. That is the positive side; now the other way, the side of *gevura*.

blocks.title: Sit there and shut up
blocks.text: The negative side: today they were bad, so instead of chapter four everybody just sits there and does nothing. "You just have to sit there and shut up." He is not teaching them anything. That breaks the plan: the curriculum he gave out says Wednesday is chapter four; it is in the blueprint. Instead they do nothing, or write lines. Why? Because that is their punishment, and the punishment is part of getting them to behave so they will study good. Who does this? The teacher: the teacher made the plan, and the teacher can break the plan.
He does not have to go by the plan: he can put in a light way too big for what was supposed to be there, an addition beyond the *kav hamida*, *davka* from the light of the Essence.

phrases.he: ולזה הטעם
כל בחינת התחדשות אור באבי''ע, הכל מעצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום דוקא
דהיינו מפני שבאורו העצמי נראה אור בקו זה
לפעמים בתוספת
ולפעמים בגרעון
phrases.en: Sometimes it's less than what you're supposed to get.

phrases.he: וכן בשינויי היחודים שבכל הפרצופים
מאדם קדמון עד עקב דאדם קדמון בסוף העשיה
כמו השינוי מזמן בית המקדש לזמן הגלות וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: Every renewal of light in *ABYA* is *davka* from the Essence above the *tzimtzum*: the *Aibershter* Himself is doing it, sometimes with more, sometimes with less. **Sometimes it's less than what you're supposed to get.** Like the Temple and the exile: how things are now is not really according to plan.

According to plan, a person is supposed to be able to get a Jewish education. People are actually not able to, even if they want to; it is not available to them. If You want people to be religious, why make a *golus* (exile) like this?

blocks.title: "I want them to suffer"
blocks.text: The same: why make these kids sit the whole day doing nothing, just suffering? "That's what I want. I want them to suffer. Because they were bad boys," so next time they won't do it no more. That is not the *kav hamida*: had everybody cooperated, it could have gone according to plan. Because they didn't, you make an extreme thing to one side; and sometimes you do it to give them extra.

blocks.title: Why the fireworks at Sinai?
blocks.text: Like the giving of the Torah: you didn't have to have all that hullabaloo. It could have been a quiet thing, Moshe off somewhere, not in front of two million people, the way most of the religions claim that some guy went to the desert and got this thing.

sensitivity.reason: Dismisses the founding claims of most other religions as "some guy went to the desert and he got this thing".

blocks.title: Why the fireworks at Sinai?
blocks.text: Why not give it to him at the burning bush? Moshe could have come to Egypt with a *Chumash* and a *Talmud* in his hand and said he had talked to the *Aibershter* in the desert. (He did talk to Him on Mount Sinai, by the way, and was told he would come back there with all the people, and then be given the Torah.) And why all the fireworks? To impress them, like taking the kids to NASA. (The student adds: and the whole going out of Egypt.)

blocks.title: Why the fireworks at Sinai?
blocks.text: But it is not just that. Neither the giving of the Torah nor the splitting of the Sea was from the *kav hamida*. The Egyptians could have dropped dead of a heart attack, or a fire burned down all the pyramids. It says He wanted *davka* to do it with water, but He could have done it another, nice way. And at Sinai the whole world was shaking, with angels flying around: not the natural order of things, which is what *kav hamida* means. Why all of that? As He told Moshe, "so that they should believe in you": to impress them, so that they will keep the Torah properly. And so too in the time of exile.

phrases.he: ודרך כלל הרי אנו אומרים יהי רצון מלפניך
מלפני עצמותך ממש,
שלמעלה מי׳ ספירות העצמיים גם כן
לשנות הרצון הפשוט שכבר נמשך בעצמות האור דאין סוף
phrases.en: We want you to change the actual *ratzon*, the *ratzon* that made the *glif glifu*. We want you to change the whole plan.

phrases.he: לבא בשיעור ששיער בעצמו עד סיום הקו,
באופן אחר,
כמו מדין לחסד וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: "May it be the will from before You": from before Your Essence, *mamash*. We are telling Him: we want You to change the actual *ratzon* (will), the *ratzon* that made the *glif glifu*. We want You to change the whole plan, as from *din* to *chesed*.

sections.title: "I have not changed": not His attributes but You
sections.summary: To ask for a new will is to ask for a change all the way back, through *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, in the measure itself. That is possible because the Essence is "not of these attributes at all": "You are the one who unifies them" means You, and the power of limit in the *kav hamida* also comes from the Essence.

phrases.he: וכנזכר לעיל (בסוף אות הט') בענין אני יהו״ה לא שניתי
בין רצון של חסד לדין באור הראשון שלפני הצמצום
מטעם הנזכר לעיל
(באות יו''ד) בענין חפץ חסד
שבעצמות ההיולי שנכלל בעצמות כו'
שיש בו ג' מדריגות עד שבא בדבר פרט כו'
(כמבואר באריכות באות י''א)

blocks.text: "I, *Havaya*, have not changed" between a will of *chesed* and of *din*: only the *tzimtzum* changes. The *chafetz chesed* has three levels until it comes into a particular thing, and we ask Him to change it all the way back at *Yachid*, so that through *Echad* and *Kadmon* to the *glif glifu* the *shiur* will be different, and so will what goes into the *reshimu* and the *Kav*.

That is what I am asking: "and He regretted", *mamash*, a change of the whole original *ratzon*. (He thinks the reference should be the end of section 8: section 5 does not talk about "I have not changed", which is really in 8 and 9.)

phrases.he: וכשאמרו אליו ולא למדותיו,
מדבר גם במדותיו העצמיים שבאור העצמות
מפני שהעצמות דאור אין סוף, לאו מכל אלין מדות כלל כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: "To Him and not to His attributes" speaks even of the essential *middos* of the *Or Ein Sof*: the Essence is "not of these attributes at all", so He can change all the *middos*.

phrases.he: וזהו
phrases.en: this is what it means

phrases.he: אנת הוא דמיחד לון כו',
אנת דוקא,
phrases.en: that means *davka* You

phrases.he: שזהו אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י׳ ספירות כו'

blocks.text: So "You are the one who unifies them": **that means *davka* You**. They are not really different things; you see them as different only because you forget about the You. When it is fierce, you are not really dealing with the *midas hadin* (the attribute of judgement): "you're really dealing with the *Aibershter*."

phrases.he: וכן מעצמות אור אין סוף דוקא בא כח הגבול והמדה
phrases.en: It's really coming from the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*

phrases.he: אשר בבחינת רשימו שבקו
שמחמת זה נקרא קו המדה
והא בהא תליה דוקא

blocks.text: The power of limit and measure in the *reshimu* in the *Kav*, which makes it the *kav hamida*: **It's really coming from the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof***. And "the one *davka* depends on the other" means that the *Aibershter* Himself is doing it.

sections.title: Two powers of equal weight, from the Essence as it is in itself
sections.summary: In the Essence there is a power to rise higher without end and a power to spread down without end, and seen from the receiver's side they swap places, like the seal in the wax. In the *Kav* the two are equal, and every more and less, weekday and Shabbos, Temple and exile, is one power divided in two. Even in a kindergarten you get the whole power of the teacher.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין כללות חסד וגבורה שבעצמות אור אין סוף
שהוא בחינת כח הגבול להגביל ולהעלים בעצמותו
בעילוי אחר עילוי עד אין קץ ושיעור
והיינו אור אין סוף למעלה עד אין קץ כו',
ובחינת התפשטות האור למטה מטה עד אין תכלית
שעל ידי הקו שנמשך מן הרשימו כו'

blocks.text: Now he calls it backwards. The power of limit, hiding in His Essence higher and higher without end, the *Or Ein Sof* above, is *gevura*; and *chesed* is the light spreading down and down, so the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* in the *Kav* are *davka* the *chesed*.

That is the rule of *mashpia* and *mekabel*: when they face each other, the right of the one is the left of the other. For the *mashpia*, the *tzimtzum* is *gevura*. For the *mekabel*, "higher and higher without end" means we don't get it, so the *Or Ein Sof* is by us a *gevura*, and the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* the *chesed*.

blocks.title: The seal in the wax
blocks.text: That is a revelation of a revelation, as he says later: the impression of a seal in wax. Put a seal in the wax and it comes out flipped around. That is the *or shel tolda*, through the *Kav* drawn from the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: וב' קוין שקולין המה בבחינת אין סוף
phrases.en: these are two exact powers, and they're both infinite

phrases.he: על כן גם בירידת האור דאין סוף בקו זה,
phrases.en: so in the *Kav*, also it's like that

phrases.he: שקולין ב' כחות הללו לצמצם ולהגביל או לחבר ולייחד
phrases.en: It has exactly the two powers, to expand or to contract; *tzimtzum* and *harchava* together are equal

blocks.text: The two lines are of equal weight, as *Ein Sof*: **these are two exact powers, and they're both infinite**. So in the descent of the light in this *Kav* too, the light and the *reshimu* are equal: the *reshimu* can limit the entire light, and the light can blot out the whole *reshimu* and fill out the whole *chalal*.
The next tape reads the lines again: **so in the *Kav*, also it's like that**. **It has exactly the two powers, to expand or to contract; *tzimtzum* and *harchava* together are equal**.

phrases.he: וכן ענין שינויי האור וההמשכה,
אם בתוספת או בגרעון,
phrases.en: whether the power to increase the light or the power to decrease the light

phrases.he: כמו מזמן לזמן, כמו מחול לשבת ויום טוב,
וכן מזמן בית המקדש לזמן הגלות,
הכל בכח א' שקול,
phrases.en: it's really one power

phrases.he: שנחלק לב' קוין חסד וגבורה
phrases.en: that is divided into two powers

phrases.he: הבא מכח ואור הראשון דעצמות אין סוף
כמו שהוא בעצמו
phrases.en: how He is in Himself

phrases.he: בבחינת חסד וגבורה כו' ודי למבין)
phrases.en: that the light and the *reshimu* are the *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*

blocks.text: The changes of the light, **whether the power to increase the light or the power to decrease the light**, weekday to Shabbos, Temple to exile, are of equal weight: **it's really one power … that is divided into two powers**, *chesed* and *gevura*. It comes from the *Atzmus Ein Sof* (not "*Or Ein Sof*", he corrects), **how He is in Himself**: the light and the *reshimu* are its *chesed* and *gevura*, the line its *tiferes*, either way round.

phrases.he: והיינו כמבואר למעלה (באות הי''ד) דקו לגבי שטח הוא היולי
phrases.en: a line is a *hiyuli* to a *shetach*

phrases.he: כולל על דרך אותו האור וכח העצמי שבעצמות של המשפיע,
רק שבעצמות הוא בהרחבת הערך ביותר,
phrases.en: In the *Atzmus*, in the *mashpia*, the *harchava* is very wide

phrases.he: ובקו זה בא כח זה עצמו בבחינת הצמצום שפע והמשכה למקבלים כו'
phrases.en: the *mekablim*: the way it goes, as the line goes down it's narrower and narrower

phrases.he: ואם כן גם בבחינת צמצום והתפשטות שבו, משם הוא בא דווקא
phrases.en: So the *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* and *hispashtus* in the *Kav* comes from the *tzimtzum* and *hispashtus* before, in the *Atzmus*

phrases.he: ודי למבין:

blocks.text: As explained above, **a line is a *hiyuli* to a *shetach***, a surface. **In the *Atzmus*, in the *mashpia*, the *harchava* is very wide**; for the *mekablim* the line gets narrower and narrower as it goes down. College students get much more of a surface than little kids, and that surface too comes from the *Kav*, in which the power of the *Atzmus* comes contracted.

So the contraction and spreading forth in the *Kav* come *davka* from there, from the contraction and spreading forth in the *Atzmus*. Even all the way down, a total *tzimtzum* and a tiny, tiny little light, it is *mamash* the power of the *Aibershter* Himself. Even "in the kindergarten, you're still getting the whole power of the teacher."

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the *Kav* come as a mere line, if it has in it the power of the first light *mamash* as the *Ein Sof*?
How do the long *nun* and the *ish tevuna* show that the lower the light goes, the higher it shows?
What are the two opposite powers in the *Kav*, and how does the prisoner who goes from the guard to the judge to the king show that they depend on each other?
Why is it a mistake to think of the *reshimu* and the *Kav* as things, and what are they really talking about?
Where does a light beyond the *kav hamida*, or a light held back, come from? Use the trip to NASA and the class that has to sit and do nothing.
